thread:
Oncall Bot: [ALERT] hosted-api-gpu-pool-1: GPU capacity exhausted and autoscaler unstable. Queue size reported > 12,400 requests. P95 latency jumping to ~18s, P99 ~47s, many 30s client timeouts. Paging infra-oncall.

Samir: I’m on it. seeing autoscaler logs show frequent scale ups to 8 then immediate scale-downs. looks like pods are being evicted due to node pressure / preemption and then HPA thinks load decreased.

Maya: Adding context — traffic spike started ~09:02 UTC from a single large customer job fanout (unified-ingest). Routed lots of long-context requests which bypassed cache and blew up token cost.

Jordan: Confirmed: queue backlog metric `hosted.requests.backlog` jumped from 300 -> 12k in ~3m. Many requests are hitting 30s gateway timeout (our default).

Samir: Quick mitigation plan:
1) apply per-route emergency throttles to reduce incoming RPS from the large tenant (temporary 60% reduction).
2) flip routing policy to favor the isolated GPU-protected pool (has a small reserve).
3) enable model-variant fallback for long requests to `rwd-compact-q4` for non-critical routes.
4) bump autoscaler maxReplicas from 10 -> 20 while we stabilize.

Samir: Running commands now:
```bash
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=worker -o wide
kubectl -n inference describe hpa hosted-gpu-workers
kubectl -n inference apply -f emergency-throttle.yaml
```

Deploy Bot: increased config `autoscaler.maxReplicas` from 10 to 20 for pool=hosted-api-gpu-pool-1 (by Samir)

Autoscale Bot: HPA event: scaled from 3 -> 8 (09:04), scaled from 8 -> 3 (09:05) due to pods failing readiness checks (eviction).

Maya: Why are pods failing readiness? logs show OOM or node-level eviction around the same time as scale-in. Possibly node autoscaler or preemptible instances getting reclaimed.

Jordan: We see `kubelet` eviction messages on nodes: memory pressure + local ephemeral disk. Some worker pods were getting SIGKILL. That causes duplicate churn and autoscaler confusion.

Samir: Immediate actions taken (09:06-09:12 UTC):
- Applied route-level throttle to `unified-ingest/*` (api-gateway) to cap concurrent requests.
- Enabled model fallback for long requests on the hosted path.
- Manually cordoned two nodes showing repeated evictions and drained workloads to healthy nodes.
- Raised GPU pool desired nodes in cloud console by +6 (emergency capacity request).

Eli: Customer-impact update: seeing 504/timeouts for a subset of customers. Top affected: Acme Analytics (heavy batch pipelines), BetaChat (chat sessions with >8k tokens). Estimated customers impacted ~7 paid customers, ~1200 failed requests in the 10m window. CS notified and triage email in progress.

Priya: Severity assessment: Service degraded for hosted API for customers with long-running requests. Recommend SEV2. Timeline: start 09:02 UTC, mitigations applied 09:06-09:12, partial recovery by 09:14. Need oncall handoff if still unstable after 09:30.

Maya: Observability notes:
- Backlog metric: `hosted.requests.backlog` peaked 12,400 at 09:05.
- P95 peaked ~18s, P99 ~47s at same time.
- Errors (gateway timeout 504) spiked to ~2.4% of requests in window.

Samir: Follow-up checks:
- We enabled KV/prefix caching on a small fraction of routes which shaved off ~20% token work for repeated prompts.
- Manual scale and node replacement stabilized evictions. backlog reduced to ~600 by 09:13.

Jordan: Still seeing occasional autoscaler flapping logs: `scale-up -> pods fail readiness -> scale-down`. We'll change HPA stabilization window to 120s to avoid oscillation.

Samir: Executed: `kubectl patch hpa hosted-gpu-workers -p '{"spec": {"behavior": {"scaleDown": {"stabilizationWindowSeconds":120}}}}'`

Deploy Bot: HPA stabilization window updated for hosted-gpu-workers (requested by Samir).

Oncall Bot: NOTE: manual intervention required to ensure node stability; cloud provider reported transient maintenance in region us-west-2 around 09:04.

Maya: Handoff plan — Samir will stay for 30m post-stable. If anything flares, escalate to infra SRE (Jordan). If stable by 09:45, handoff to Maya for monitoring.

Samir: Handoff summary for next oncall:
- Root cause: sudden heavy tokenized load from single tenant + node-level evictions causing autoscaler oscillation and effective capacity reduction.
- Current state: backlog ~120, p95 ~1200ms, p99 ~3.2s, GPU node count increased temporary to absorb current demand.
- Actions to complete: verify cloud nodes no longer preemptible; set node pool eviction protection; follow up with cloud infra to get replacement nodes out of maintenance.

Eli: CS will follow up with affected customers and provide timeline and mitigation notes.

Priya: Post-incident tasks assigned:
- (Samir) Root-cause writeup and timeline (due EOD).
- (Jordan) Autoscaler tuning PR and add stabilization policy tests.
- (Maya) Add early-detection alert for queue growth correlated with single-tenant high-token ratio.
- (Eli) Customer communications draft.

Samir: Creating incident doc: `INC-2026-1801234567-gpu-exhaustion-hosted` and will attach logs and artifacts.

Maya: Taking over monitoring now. If anything changes, ping @Maya and escalate to @Jordan. :thumbsup:

Oncall Bot: Handoff recorded: Samir -> Maya at 09:20 UTC.

Jordan: quick note — consider adding a circuit-breaker that rejects >X tokens for a single request or routes it to an offline batch job path. This would prevent single-tenant blowups in the future.

Samir: Agreed. Adding as action item in postmortem.

Eli: Customer impact summary so far (for postmortem): ~7 customers affected, approx 1200 failed requests, no data loss, primary impact was latency/timeouts.

Priya: Closing loop: severity SEV2, P0 mitigations done, owners assigned. We'll reconvene for RCA tomorrow.

Maya: Closing thread for now, monitoring 30m. Thanks all. :heart:
